newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Futures trade leads S.African industrials to close.
newsitem.headline: Futures trade leads S.African industrials to close.

text.p: South African industrial shares shunned Wall Street's rich overnight gains to trade weaker on Friday morning before being pulled higher by futures trade to finish strong, dealers said.
They said that the South African market was exceptionally volatile at the moment because it as dominated by futures-related trade, which could knock shares down or build them up at will.
In early trade industrials were dragged down by futures players and not even a strong close on Wall Street could buoy them, but in afternoon trade futures-related trade pushed industrials up.
Industrials finished the day 40.7 points higher at 8,003.3.
Dealers said the local market was very volatile and that, in addition to futures trade, this was largely due to the number of large, one-off deals like asset swaps taking place.
They, together with portfolio managers said that industrials had been under a great deal of pressure.
Looking ahead some market commentators said that the market was enjoying some reasonably good economic indicators which should ensure firmer industrial shares next week.
But others said that another large asset swap could be about to take place, which would weigh the market.
Still, strength on the industrial board helped the all-share index up and it closed 17.9 points higher at 6,676.1.
Gold shares struggled throughout the day to stifle their fall on the back of dull bullion.
Dealers said that it was unlikely these shares would enjoy any recovery, however mild, in the near future.
The bullion price fell overnight and knocked shares down, but its tiny recovery in the afternoon halted their fall.
The gold index finished 15.3 points lower at 1,350.0.
